Subject: Post-call: Redwood + Acme — stakeholder map & procurement next steps

Hi John (and procurement team),

Great to meet earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

- Economic buyer: John Stevens (you) — interested in predictable inference costs and dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive models.
- Technical champion: Sophie Lin (ML infra) — will own the PoC and performance validation.
- Procurement: standard PO + legal review; timeline target: procurement sign-off by Nov 15.

Key decision criteria we heard:
- Cost per token and predictable monthly spend for production workloads
- SLA commitment for uptime (customer expects 99.9% or better)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 report, data residency assurances, and audit logs

Acme asked about two exceptions they need for internal buying process:
1) A one-time first-year discount of 20% tied to volume commit (expected ARR ~$1.2M)
2) A short SLA amendment to include a 99.9% uptime target and credits for outages (they will request this in their contract template)

Attached: draft SOW (Acme_SOW_v2.pdf) and a pricing workbook.

John — can you confirm procurement timeline and any mandatory legal terms they require?

Internal: Aditya — can you confirm the technical fit and whether the PoC (dedicated pool) is feasible on our side for the proposed timeline?

I expect I'll need to route a procurement/discount exception internally; looping in Lauren and Finance for approval. Appreciate quick responses — procurement is meeting on Nov 12 and we'd like to have our ask pre-cleared.

Thanks,
Marissa
